references.text: Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan and camped outside the city, where he bought the plot of land that was later given to Joseph. See [ref:1 Mos 33:18-19|Genesis 33:18-19].

Jacob gave Joseph a plot of land (Shechem) that he had taken from the Amorites – this is the same plot of land that John connects with Jesus' meeting with the Samaritan woman. See [ref:1 Mos 48:22|Genesis 48:22].

Joseph's bones, which the Israelites had brought with them from Egypt, were buried in Shechem, on the plot of land that Jacob had bought. This confirms the connection between Sychar/Shechem and Joseph's inheritance. See [ref:Jos 24:32|Joshua 24:32].

The Samaritan woman herself mentions that the well was given to them by "our father Jacob," which directly links the conversation to the plot of land Jacob gave to Joseph. See [ref:Joh 4:12|John 4:12].
Jacob's well was located right at this plot of land, and Jesus sat down there. The well is the concrete place connected with Jacob's gift to Joseph. See [ref:Joh 4:6|John 4:6].

Stephen's speech refers to how Jacob and the fathers were brought to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought, linking the history of the patriarchs to this place. See [ref:Apg 7:15-16|Acts 7:15-16].

Abram traveled through the land to Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh, and the Lord appeared to him there. Shechem was already an important spiritual place from the time of the patriarchs. See [ref:1 Mos 12:6-7|Genesis 12:6-7].
